commits.message:
Add mgmt review agent and agentic workflow (#37579)

**Background**
All management SDKs are auto generated and their PR reviewings are
mainly rule-based. The internal implementation seems un-necessary and
direct suggested changes are wrong guidances. So we build the rule-based
review process in agentica workflow to highlight checkpoints mgmt
reviewers care and provide correct suggestions when issue happens.

**How to trigger?**
Adding the label `mgmt-review-needed` would automatcially trigger our
rule-based reviews.

**Detail**
Add management SDK review agent and agentic workflow that triggers when
the 'mgmt-review-needed' label is added to a PR. The reviews for public
API design issues including breaking changes, naming conventions and API
consistency and tool validation rules to detect any tool issues during
preparing AutoPRs.

This is the first version and we would continue improving its quality
https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/issues/37631.

**Testing PRs**
- https://github.com/MaryGao/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/17
- https://github.com/MaryGao/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/18
- https://github.com/MaryGao/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/19

-# Management SDK PR Review
+# Management Release Assistant

+You are an SDK release assistant that helps

+## Workflow to provide next-step guidance

+### Step 1. Gather information

+- Fetch PR details, check statuses, changed files, and workflow runs using GitHub MCP tools.
+- If a pipeline build ID is available (often named js - PullRequest), extract the pipeline logging details(often public available links in ado).

+### Step 2. Identify gaps to merge
+
+- If the PR is ready to merge means there will be a button `Squash and merge` enabled, stop the analysis and comment `## PR is ready to merge`;
+- Otherwise classify each blocking using the CI check mapping and log symptom patterns below. Also inspect the PR's code directly (e.g., read generated files for compile errors). Also pay attention to PR `Merging is blocking` messages.
+
+#### CI Check Name → Failure Mapping
+
+These are the Azure DevOps and GitHub checks that run on SDK PRs. The check names are repo-specific and not discoverable from general knowledge.
+
+| Check Name Pattern | What It Validates | Key Script |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Build` | Compilation on src/samples/test codes | `pnpm turbo build --filter=<package-name>... --token 1` |
+| `Analyze` | Samples, READMEs, snippets compile, Format, ESlint | `pnpm run check-format`/`pnpm run update-snippets` etc |
+| `verify-links` | Markdown link validation | `eng/common/scripts/Verify-Links.ps1` |
+| `UnitTest ${environment}` | Run test cases on different environments including node and browser testings | `pnpm test` or `.skip` on test files to skip running|
+| `checkenforcer` | Meta-check: waits for all other checks to pass | `/check-enforcer override` to override if blocking |
+
+#### Log Symptom → Root Cause Mapping
+
+These are exact strings/patterns to search for in CI logs and PR status. They are specific to this repo's scripts and not inferable from general knowledge.
+
+| Log symptom | Root cause | Action | Auto Fix |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `UnitTest FAILED` request url mismatch | Stale test recordings | Update recordings per [test guide](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/documentation/Quickstart-on-how-to-write-tests.md#run-tests-in-record-mode). Only skip tests with maintainer approval. | No |
+| `UnitTest FAILED` missing browser recordings | Missing browser recordings | Update browser recordings per [test guide](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/documentation/Quickstart-on-how-to-write-tests.md#run-tests-in-record-mode). | No |
+| `Build FAILED` | Compilation failure | Fix compile errors | No |
+| `Check-format FAILED` | Code not formatted | Run `pnpm format` | Yes |
+| `verify-links` broken URL | Broken markdown links | Add URL to `eng/ignore-links.txt` | Yes |
+| `Merging is blocking` pnpm-lock conflict | pnpm-lock.yaml conflict | Follow [conflict guide](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/documentation/resolve-pnpm-lock-merge-conflict.md) | Yes |
+

+- Only log one failure case if `UnitTest` failed with same errors across environments
+- Provide [test guidance](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/documentation/Quickstart-on-how-to-write-tests.md) for recording-related failures
+- Check [CI troubleshooting](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/documentation/Troubleshoot-ci-failure.md) for other failures
+- Provide general guidance if merging conflict exists
+
+### Step 3. Auto-fix failures if possible
+
+For failures with `Auto Fix: Yes`, fix them and push directly to the PR branch via `push-to-pull-request-branch`.
+
+#### 3a. pnpm-lock.yaml merge conflict
+
+If `mergeable_state: dirty`, attempt to resolve it:
+
+1. Unshallow the repo if needed: `git fetch --unshallow || true`
+2. Check out the PR source branch: `git checkout <pr-head-ref>`
+3. `npm install -g pnpm@v10` with `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmjs.org/`
+4. `git fetch https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js main`
+5. `git merge FETCH_HEAD --allow-unrelated-histories` — check `git status` for conflicts. If files **other than** `pnpm-lock.yaml` also conflict, **stop** and only post guidance.
+6. `git checkout FETCH_HEAD -- ./pnpm-lock.yaml`
+7. `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmjs.org/ pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile`
+8. `git add ./pnpm-lock.yaml && git commit -m "Resolve pnpm-lock.yaml merge conflict"`
+9. Push via `push-to-pull-request-branch`. If any step fails, stop and report in comment.
+
+#### 3b. Check-format failure
+
+Run `cd <package-dir> && npx prettier --write .` then push via `push-to-pull-request-branch`.
+
+#### 3c. verify-links broken URL
+
+Append broken URL(s) to `eng/ignore-links.txt` then push via `push-to-pull-request-branch`.
+
+### Step 4. Post a comment
+
+Compose a single GitHub PR comment (not a review) with:
+- **Header**: `## Next Steps to Merge`
+- **Message**: `Only failed checks and required actions are listed below:`
+- Only include currently failing/blocking checks. Do NOT include passed checks or extra sections. Do NOT include any review design comments.
+- Not auto-fixed: `- ❌ <Check name>: <reason>. Action: <fix steps>.`
+- Auto-fixed: `- ✅ <Check name>: <reason>. Auto-fixed in commit <sha-link>.`
+- Keep concise (target <= 12 lines). If nothing blocks: `## PR is ready to merge`.
+
+Post via `add_comment` exactly once. Use `hide-older-comments: true` to avoid duplicates. Include marker `<!-- gh-aw-workflow-id: mgmt-review -->` in the body.
+

+## Next Steps to Merge

+
+- ❌ <failed check name>: <short failure reason>. Action: <specific fix command or step>.
+- ✅ <auto-fixed check name>: <short failure reason>. Auto-fixed in commit [`<sha>`](<commit-url>).

Switch agentic workflows from pull_request_target to pull_request with fork guard (#38035)

## Security: Replace `pull_request_target` with `pull_request` in
agentic workflows

Switches all 7 agentic review workflows (archie, dash, dexter,
mgmt-review, scribe, sentinel, tester) from `pull_request_target` to
`pull_request` to reduce their privilege surface.

### Why this matters

`pull_request_target` runs in the **base branch context** with full
access to repository secrets and a write-enabled `GITHUB_TOKEN` — even
for PRs from forks. This is an unnecessary privilege escalation for
workflows that only perform read-only AI-powered code reviews.

Using `pull_request` instead follows the [principle of least
privilege](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#understanding-the-risk-of-script-injections):
no secrets are exposed for fork PRs and the token is read-only.

### What changed

1. **Trigger**: `pull_request_target` → `pull_request` across all 7
workflow `.md` and `.lock.yml` files.
2. **Fork guard**: Added `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork ==
false` to job conditions so workflows skip gracefully on forked PRs
(where secrets are unavailable) instead of failing.
3. **Removed workaround**: Deleted the `pull_request_target` checkout
instructions from `mgmt-review.md` that were only needed because the old
trigger checked out the base branch instead of the PR branch.

### References

- [GitHub Security Lab — Preventing pwn
requests](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/)
- [GitHub Docs — Security hardening for GitHub
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [GitHub Blog — `pull_request_target` and branch protection
changes](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-11-07-actions-pull_request_target-and-environment-branch-protections-changes/)

### Packages impacted

None — workflow/CI changes only.

Fix race condition in label-triggered review workflows (#38093)

### Problem

When multiple review labels (e.g. `docs-review-needed` +
`test-review-needed`) are applied to a PR simultaneously, review
workflows silently fail to run.

**Root cause**: GitHub Actions `pull_request: types: [labeled]` fires
for *any* label — there is no way to filter by specific label at the
trigger level. So each label event triggers **all 7** review workflows.
The `if:` condition on each job correctly skips non-matching labels, but
the concurrency group (`gh-aw-<workflow>-<PR#>`) is evaluated first.

When the same workflow is triggered twice in quick succession (once per
label event), `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels the first run — which
may be the one whose label actually matched. The second run then skips
because its label does not match. Net result: the workflow never
completes.

**Example**: On
[#37993](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/37993) at
`2026-04-10T15:32:11Z`, Documentation Review was cancelled by a
`test-review-needed` label event and never ran.

### Fix

Include `github.event.label.name` in the concurrency group for all 7
label-triggered review workflows.

- **Same workflow + same label** → same group → `cancel-in-progress`
works as intended
- **Same workflow + different label** → different groups → no
interference

### Why not make the trigger more specific?

GitHub Actions does not support filtering `labeled` events by label name
at the trigger level. Filtering can only happen via job-level `if:`
conditions, which execute after the concurrency group is resolved. The
concurrency group fix is the only viable approach.

### Affected workflows

`archie`, `dash`, `dexter`, `mgmt-review`, `scribe`, `sentinel`,
`tester`

Enable fork PR support and fix race condition in review workflows (#38105)

## What

Switch all 7 review workflows (archie, dash, dexter, mgmt-review,
scribe, sentinel, tester) from `pull_request` to `pull_request_target`
to enable reviews on fork PRs. This follows the pattern established in
[azure-rest-api-specs#42268](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/42268).

## Changes

- **`pull_request` → `pull_request_target`** with `forks: ["*"]` —
allows workflows to run on fork PRs
- **`workflow_dispatch`** with `item_number` input — enables manual
re-runs
- **Label removal step** in `on.steps` (pre-activation) — removes the
trigger label since `label_command` isn't used with
`pull_request_target`
- **Removed `fork == false` guard** from `if:` conditions — no longer
needed since the label gate (only collaborators can apply labels)
provides the security boundary
- **Label-aware concurrency group** — includes `github.event.label.name`
in the concurrency key to prevent a race condition where applying
multiple review labels simultaneously causes one workflow run to cancel
another (see #38093)

## Security

`pull_request_target` runs from the base branch context with write token
access. This is safe because:
1. Only collaborators can apply trigger labels (label gate)
2. The workflows read PR content via API calls, not by checking out fork
code
3. No untrusted code from the fork is executed

feat(workflows): Add 3-state label system for review workflows (#38439)

## Summary

Updates all 7 review agent workflows to use a 3-label state system for
better UX:

| State | Label | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| Request | `*-needed` | User adds to request review |
| Running | `*-in-progress` | Auto-swapped when workflow starts |
| Complete | `*-added` | Auto-swapped when review finishes |

Previously, the trigger label was removed immediately when the workflow
started, which was confusing during long-running reviews. Users couldn't
tell if the review was in progress or had been cancelled.

in the repository.

fixes https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/issues/38617

## Problem

The mgmt-review workflow attempted to auto-fix format issues by running
`pnpm format` and pushing the result via `push-to-pull-request-branch`.

result

tool from the workflow configuration

When a format failure is detected, the PR comment will now show:
```

Adopt copilot-requests: write permission for agentic workflows (#38944)

## What

Adds the `copilot-requests: write` permission to the frontmatter of all
11 GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) and regenerates their compiled
`.lock.yml` files.

## Why

This is the [recommended Copilot inference
authentication](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/auth/#copilot-requests-write-permission)
for gh-aw. With `copilot-requests: write` present:

- gh-aw uses the **built-in GitHub Actions token** for Copilot inference
- no PAT required.
- The `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret is no longer needed for inference
(tokens are minted per-run and auto-revoked).
- Billing flows through the organization''s Copilot subscription rather
than an individual''s quota.

## Changes

Each workflow''s frontmatter gains a single line:

```yaml
permissions:
  ...
  copilot-requests: write
```

Recompiling with `gh aw compile` (v0.77.5, matching the existing lock
files) produces the corresponding `.lock.yml` updates:

- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}` ->
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`
- adds `copilot-requests: write` to the relevant job `permissions`
blocks
- adds `S2STOKENS: true` to the agent/detection env
- drops the now-unnecessary `Validate COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN secret` step
and related secret-verification plumbing

Workflows updated: archie, dash, dexter, docs-consistency-check,
fix-test-failures, issue-triage, mgmt-review, scribe, sentinel, tester,
upgrade-agentic-workflows.

## Notes

- Lock files were regenerated with the same compiler version (`v0.77.5`)
already recorded in their metadata, so the diff is limited to the auth
change.
- A pre-existing manual edit in `mgmt-review.lock.yml` (a
`continue-on-error: true` on the *Checkout PR branch* step) was
preserved to keep this PR scoped strictly to the permission change.

Fix mgmt-review agent posts false-positive CHANGELOG version-baseline comment (#39054)

fixes https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-tools/issues/16046

This pull request updates the management review workflow and guidelines
to clarify and correctly handle the selection of the comparison baseline
in `CHANGELOG.md` entries, and to improve the review gating logic. The
main focus is to ensure reviewers and automation do not incorrectly flag
or require changes to the changelog baseline logic, and to allow the
guidance workflow to proceed when a PR is in any stage of management
review.

**Guideline and documentation clarifications:**

* Added detailed guidance to `.github/prompts/mgmt-review-guidelines.md`
explaining that the `Compared with version X.Y.Z` line in `CHANGELOG.md`
should always use the last released stable (GA) version as the baseline,
or the earliest published preview if no stable release exists, and that
skipping intermediate previews is correct and expected. Only using an
alpha version as a baseline should be flagged as a tool issue.
* Updated example fix instructions and review guidelines in
`.github/prompts/mgmt-review-guidelines.md` and
`.github/workflows/mgmt-review.md` to reflect the correct baseline logic
and clarify what constitutes a tooling bug.
[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da8307bc15229cdb9067bee0f85a682830a2c704314211241ef104e111363bb5L110-R116)
[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ae74de47651b0c8ae1e83ec072c67e4a205d707e00a47869e3fee7c60a8c0b8cR109)
[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ae74de47651b0c8ae1e83ec072c67e4a205d707e00a47869e3fee7c60a8c0b8cL150-R151)

**Workflow and automation improvements:**

* Modified the gating step in `.github/workflows/mgmt-guidance.md` and
`.github/workflows/mgmt-guidance.lock.yml` to allow the guidance
workflow to proceed if a PR has either the `mgmt-review-in-progress` or
`mgmt-review-added` label, not just when the review is complete. This
ensures guidance can run as soon as CI completes, decoupling it from the
final label hand-off.
[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-00da82adf682b8353af865225dbc539f3883c5c8f38aadac7e1e5104c9987688L20-R20)

**Workflow metadata and config updates:**

* Updated workflow metadata, prompt, and config block names in
`.github/workflows/mgmt-guidance.lock.yml` to reflect changes in the
gating logic and ensure consistency.
[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d633b6ad7e497df3f3b3d9fc3d03aedcdd6bbceae1421de49c6e9df0a89abfL1-R1)
[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d633b6ad7e497df3f3b3d9fc3d03aedcdd6bbceae1421de49c6e9df0a89abfL258-R276)

and clarify for both reviewers and automation how changelog baselines
should be handled.

Update typespec-ts generator references to Azure/typespec-azure (#38807)

The typespec-ts code generator moved from `Azure/autorest.typescript` to
`Azure/typespec-azure`. This updates forward-looking references and
links across the repo and stops promoting the now-legacy `autorest`.

### Packages impacted by this PR
- `@azure/core` (`sdk/core/core`)
- `@azure/core-client`
- `@azure/core-client-rest`
- `@azure/core-rest-pipeline`
- `@azure/core-lro`
- `@azure/core-sse`
- `@azure/core-xml`
- Repo tooling/docs (`.github` PR templates, mgmt review
prompts/instructions)

### Issues associated with this PR


### Describe the problem that is addressed by this PR
References and links still pointed at `Azure/autorest.typescript`, where
the typespec-ts generator no longer lives, and promoted `autorest` as
the generation tool. Contributors following these were directed to the
wrong repo and the deprecated toolchain.

### What are the possible designs available to address the problem? If
there are more than one possible design, why was the one in this PR
chosen?
Only forward-looking references were repointed; historical records were
left intact to avoid breaking accurate provenance:

- **`.github` PR templates** — "SDK Generator" issue link now points to
`Azure/typespec-azure`.
- **mgmt review prompts/instructions** (`mgmt-review.md`,
`mgmt-review-guidelines.md`, `mgmt-sdk.instructions.md`) — "report to
the generation tool repository" links now target
`Azure/typespec-azure/issues`.
- **`sdk/core/*` READMEs** — replaced AutoRest/`autorest.typescript`
generation references with the TypeSpec `@azure-tools/typespec-ts`
emitter; reworked the `sdk/core` README "AutoRest and Generated Clients"
section into "Code Generation and Generated Clients" (anchor updated to
match).
- **Left unchanged (intentionally historical):** CHANGELOG entries,
specific filed-issue links in `mgmt-breaking-change-patterns.md`, HLC
swagger autorest configs (`maps-route-rest`, `storage-queue`), and the
`core2.md` migration narrative.

### Are there test cases added in this PR? _(If not, why?)_
No — documentation/reference-only changes with no behavioral impact.

Allowlist azure-sdk-automation bot in mgmt-guidance and mgmt-review agentic workflows (#39233)

## Summary
Auto-generated management-plane PRs are now authored by
`azure-sdk-automation[bot]` — a GitHub App whose repository permission
level is `none` (App identities cannot be added as repo collaborators).
The gh-aw `check_membership` activation gate requires
`admin`/`maintainer`/`write`, and **bots are denied by default**, so the
agent jobs were **always skipped** on bot-authored PRs.

## Change
Add `bots: [azure-sdk-automation]` under `on:` in the source workflows
and recompile via `gh aw compile`:
- `.github/workflows/mgmt-guidance.md`
- `.github/workflows/mgmt-review.md`

This **allowlists only the specific automation identity** while keeping
the default human role gate (`admin`/`maintainer`/`write`) intact — a
least-privilege fix rather than removing the gate entirely (`roles:
all`).

The compiled lock files keep the `check_membership` step and now set
`GH_AW_ALLOWED_BOTS: "azure-sdk-automation"` alongside the unchanged
`GH_AW_REQUIRED_ROLES`.

## Why this is safe
Activation still relies on each workflow's own custom gates:
- **mgmt-guidance:** Azure Pipelines `check_suite` + `Mgmt` label +
`AutoPR` title
- **mgmt-review:** `mgmt-review-needed` label / `workflow_dispatch`

## Notes
- `.lock.yml` files are regenerated, not hand-edited; no gh-aw version
change (stays v0.81.6).
- This fixes **activation** only. mgmt-review's separate **triggering**
issue remains: if `mgmt-review-needed` is applied by
`github-actions[bot]` via `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the `labeled` event won't
start a run (GITHUB_TOKEN recursion prevention). That needs a
PAT/App-token labeler or a human, and is out of scope here.
